_comment: THE CATEGORY MENU — the seven published public-benefit categories of the statutes,
Art. 7 (ops decision D33 item 1), confirmed at the founding assembly. This is the ONLY
category vocabulary a registry record, an artifact or a public surface may name: a
category that is not on this list would be a fabricated fact about where money goes. A
category is the basket of listed recipients assigned to it and nothing else, which is
why the word to prefer is "category" rather than "fund".
PUBLISHED ONCE, VENDORED. The canonical copy is examples/category-menu.v1.example.json
in the contract repository, validated there against schemas/category-menu.v1.json and
against the slug set of schemas/registry-v0-record.v1.json. The curated registry
repository holds a BYTE-IDENTICAL vendored copy at config/category-funds.json, so that
repository validates with nothing but its own checkout, and its CI checks out the public
contract repository and fails on any byte difference. Vendor, then assert equality — one
list, never two kept level by convention.
`category_id` keeps the `cat-*` form the ledger's `category_fund_id` column uses and must
equal `cat-{slug}` for every entry. JSON Schema cannot express that agreement, so both
repositories' gates assert it.
PROVISIONAL. The category NAMES are published. `provisional` stays true because the
Recipient List — the named organisations inside each category — is adopted at the founding
assembly and published as the versioned annex to the statutes; no recipient is listed yet.
Flip it to false when that annex is published, and never before.
